youtube.title: Rust Day 8: Tuples & Arrays Explained 🦀 #Shorts

scenes.say: Rust, day eight. Two ways to group values together: tuples and arrays.

scenes.heading: Tuples
scenes.say: A tuple groups values of different types: an integer, a float and a char, and its length is fixed. You can destructure it into a, b and c, or grab one item with dot zero.
scenes.captions: A tuple groups values of different types: an integer, a float and a char, and its length is fixed. You can destructure it into a, b and c, or grab one item with .0

scenes.heading: Positions start at 0
scenes.say: Positions start at zero: tup dot zero, dot one, dot two.

scenes.heading: Arrays
scenes.say: An array holds values of one type, with a fixed length. zero semicolon three makes three zeros. a of zero reads the first element, and len gives the length.
scenes.captions: An array holds values of one type, with a fixed length. [0; 3] makes three zeros. a[0] reads the first element, and len() gives the length.

scenes.heading: What it prints
scenes.say: So it prints one, five, and three zeros.
scenes.captions: So it prints 1, 5, and three zeros.

scenes.heading: Common mistake
scenes.say: Now the classic mistake: index five of a three element array.

scenes.heading: Caught at compile time
scenes.caption: index out of bounds
scenes.say: Rust stops it: index out of bounds, the length is 3 but the index is 5. If the index is only known at runtime, the program panics instead of reading random memory.

scenes.heading: Recap
scenes.say: Recap: tuples mix types, arrays hold one type, both have a fixed length, and indexes start at zero.
